task.description: Gate docs/agents/design/REQ-003.md per WF-02 Step 1b. Read the design artefact independently (do not read CODE-DESIGNER's handoff result.summary as a substitute). CODE-DESIGNER's design (PASS) proposes: (1) append 'en' to src/i18n/routing.ts's locales array, defaultLocale stays 'ru'; (2) create messages/en.json matching messages/ru.json's 177-leaf-key structure exactly, values duplicated verbatim from ru.json as placeholders; (3) no code change needed to src/i18n/request.ts, src/components/landing/LocaleSwitcher.tsx, or src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx (all already generic over routing.locales) — verify this claim yourself by reading those three files directly, don't take it on trust. One open question was flagged in the design: Metadata.ogLocale's placeholder value — the design proposes 'en_US' by analogy to REQ-001a's ru_RU/uz_UZ precedent, but REQ-003's own requirement text doesn't name this value explicitly. Decide whether this is an acceptable design choice (stated open question, reasonable analogy, not silently resolved) or whether it needs to route back to CODE-DESIGNER/ORCH for an explicit decision before FRONTEND-DEV builds it.

result.summary: docs/agents/design/REQ-003.md gated PASS. Read the design artefact independently (not CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary). Checked against WF-02 Step 1b: (a) every acceptance criterion maps to a concrete design element via §6's table, no TBD/deferral language present; §5's open questions are genuinely undetermined items with proposed resolutions, not deferrals of required work; (b) props/types check is n/a — no new component in scope (only a new data file, messages/en.json, plus a one-line array edit in routing.ts) — design states this explicitly rather than silently skipping it, confirmed correct by independent read of all three 'unchanged' files; (c) every CSS/token reference (.lang, .lang a, .lang .on, var(--primary), var(--muted), var(--border)) verified present at the cited lines in src/app/globals.css — no invented token, and no false claim of resolving against docs/Design system for AI agents/tokens/tokens.css (that file defines no --mono/--muted/--primary/--border at all; this switcher correctly stays on globals.css's own bespoke vars, matching REQ-001a's established precedent); (d) no implementation code present — scanned full artefact, only file tree, structural-shape pseudocode, JSON key-shape description, and prose. 'No code change needed' claims independently re-verified by reading the three files directly (not taken from the design doc): src/i18n/request.ts line 13 loads messages via a template literal keyed off the resolved locale with no ru/uz literal; src/components/landing/LocaleSwitcher.tsx line 13 maps over routing.locales with no hardcoded locale literal or fixed-length destructuring; src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx lines 33/46/62 read locale/Metadata.ogLocale/routing.locales generically via getTranslations/hasLocale. Also independently verified messages/ru.json actually has 13 top-level namespaces and 177 leaf keys (via a script, not inspection) as the design claims. ogLocale open question resolved explicitly (not passed through): en_US is accepted as the correct placeholder value — it is the standard OpenGraph/HTTP locale-code form for English, directly analogous to the already-accepted ru_RU/uz_UZ pair from REQ-001a's design (verified by reading docs/agents/design/REQ-001a.md §2, which used the identical reasoning and was previously gated PASS), and duplicating ru_RU verbatim into en.json would emit a factually wrong OpenGraph locale tag — a metadata-correctness bug, not translation content, so it isn't covered by REQ-004's translation-scope carve-out. The design correctly flagged this as an open question with a reasoned proposal rather than silently picking a value, which is the correct Step-1 behavior, not a defect requiring rework.
